33:36.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنࣲ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡۗ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
33:36.en: And it becometh not a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His messenger have decided an affair (for them), that they should (after that) claim any say in their affair; and whoso is rebellious to Allah and His messenger, he verily goeth astray in error manifest

33:72.ar: إِنَّا عَرَضۡنَا ٱلۡأَمَانَةَ عَلَى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱلۡجِبَالِ فَأَبَيۡنَ أَن يَحۡمِلۡنَهَا وَأَشۡفَقۡنَ مِنۡهَا وَحَمَلَهَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ ظَلُومࣰ ا جَهُولࣰ ا
33:72.en: Lo! We offered the trust unto the heavens and the earth and the hills, but they shrank from bearing it and were afraid of it. And man assumed it. Lo! he hath proved a tyrant and a fool

34:24.ar: ۞قُلۡ مَن يَرۡزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ قُلِ ٱللَّهُۖ وَإِنَّآ أَوۡ إِيَّاكُمۡ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوۡ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
34:24.en: Say: Who giveth you provision from the sky and the earth? Say: Allah, Lo! we or you assuredly are rightly guided or in error manifest

34:46.ar: ۞قُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَعِظُكُم بِوَٰحِدَةٍۖ أَن تَقُومُواْ لِلَّهِ مَثۡنَىٰ وَفُرَٰدَىٰ ثُمَّ تَتَفَكَّرُواْۚ مَا بِصَاحِبِكُم مِّن جِنَّةٍۚ إِنۡ هُوَ إِلَّا نَذِيرࣱ لَّكُم بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡ عَذَابࣲ شَدِيدࣲ‏
34:46.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): I exhort you unto one thing only: that ye awake, for Allah's sake, by twos and singly, and then reflect: There is no madness in your comrade. He is naught else than a warner unto you in face of a terrific doom

35:27.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا بِهِۦ ثَمَرَٰتࣲ مُّخۡتَلِفًا أَلۡوَٰنُهَاۚ وَمِنَ ٱلۡجِبَالِ جُدَدُۢ بِيضࣱ وَحُمۡرࣱ مُّخۡتَلِفٌ أَلۡوَٰنُهَا وَغَرَابِيبُ سُودࣱ‏
35:27.en: Hast thou not seen that Allah causeth water to fall from the sky, and We produce therewith fruit of divers hues; and among the hills are streaks white and red, of divers hues, and (others) raven-black

35:28.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَٱلدَّوَآبِّ وَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ مُخۡتَلِفٌ أَلۡوَٰنُهُۥ كَذَٰلِكَۗ إِنَّمَا يَخۡشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِ ٱلۡعُلَمَٰٓؤُاْۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ غَفُورٌ
35:28.en: And of men and beasts and cattle, in like manner, divers hues? The erudite among His bondmen fear Allah alone. Lo! Allah is Mighty, Forgiving

36:20.ar: وَجَآءَ مِنۡ أَقۡصَا ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ رَجُلࣱ يَسۡعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱتَّبِعُواْ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ
36:20.en: And there came from the uttermost part of the city a man running. He cried: O my people! Follow those who have been sent

36:21.ar: ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَن لَّا يَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ أَجۡرࣰ ا وَهُم مُّهۡتَدُونَ
36:21.en: Follow those who ask of you no fee, and who are rightly guided

36:22.ar: وَمَالِيَ لَآ أَعۡبُدُ ٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنِي وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
36:22.en: For what cause should I not serve Him Who hath created me, and unto Whom ye will be brought back

36:23.ar: ءَأَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ ءَالِهَةً إِن يُرِدۡنِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ بِضُرࣲّ لَّا تُغۡنِ عَنِّي شَفَٰعَتُهُمۡ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يُنقِذُونِ
36:23.en: Shall I take (other) gods in place of Him when, if the Beneficent should wish me any harm, their intercession will avail me naught, nor can they save

36:24.ar: إِنِّيٓ إِذࣰ ا لَّفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينٍ
36:24.en: Then truly I should be in error manifest

36:25.en: Lo! I have believed in your Lord, so hear me

36:26.ar: قِيلَ ٱدۡخُلِ ٱلۡجَنَّةَۖ قَالَ يَٰلَيۡتَ قَوۡمِي يَعۡلَمُونَ
36:26.en: It was said (unto him): Enter paradise. He said: Would that my people knew

36:27.ar: بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمُكۡرَمِينَ
36:27.en: With what (munificence) my Lord hath pardoned me and made me of the honoured ones

2:185.ar: شَهۡرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ هُدࣰ ى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَٱلۡفُرۡقَانِۚ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ ٱلشَّهۡرَ فَلۡيَصُمۡهُۖ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرࣲ فَعِدَّةࣱ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۗ يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡيُسۡرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡعُسۡرَ وَلِتُكۡمِلُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:185.en: The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind, and clear proofs of the guidance, and the Criterion (of right and wrong). And whosoever of you is present, let him fast the month, and whosoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast the same) number of other days. Allah desireth for you ease; He desireth not hardship for you; and (He desireth) that ye should complete the period, and that ye should magnify Allah for having guided you, and that peradventure ye may be thankful

22:78.ar: وَجَٰهِدُواْ فِي ٱللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِۦۚ هُوَ ٱجۡتَبَىٰكُمۡ وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ مِنۡ حَرَجࣲۚ مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمۡ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَۚ هُوَ سَمَّىٰكُمُ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ مِن قَبۡلُ وَفِي هَٰذَا لِيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ شَهِيدًا عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِۚ فَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱعۡتَصِمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ هُوَ مَوۡلَىٰكُمۡۖ فَنِعۡمَ ٱلۡمَوۡلَىٰ وَنِعۡمَ ٱلنَّصِيرُ
22:78.en: And strive for Allah with the endeavour which is His right. He hath chosen you and hath not laid upon you in religion any hardship; the faith of your father Abraham (is yours). He hath named you Muslims of old time and in this (Scripture), that the messenger may be a witness against you, and that ye may be witnesses against mankind. So establish worship, pay the poor-due, and hold fast to Allah. He is your Protecting friend. A blessed Patron and a blessed Helper

Ph84HVFLfvs.one_line: On obedience to Allah: no option once He decrees, choice as the trust humans carried, debating by evidence, deep reflection, science and reverence.
Ph84HVFLfvs.summary: He introduces a cluster on submission: al-Ahzab on obeying when it is hardest, Saba on how communities obey, Fatir on obeying through knowledge, and Ya-Sin on obedience as the route to real life. The central verse of al-Ahzab says a believer does not treat Allah's decree as optional; commands are never harmful, and what feels hard is our own selfishness. The trust refused by the heavens, earth and mountains is freedom of choice, which only humans have, which is why reward and punishment exist; he urges parents to let children face the consequences of their choices. From Saba he argues that communities survive through healthy dialogue, and that the Quran's 'either we or you are guided' expresses a creed that follows evidence and accepts nothing blindly, since only certainty holds in hardship. The one piece of advice in Saba is to dedicate oneself to Allah and reflect deeply, because behaviour follows inner conviction, as the Prophet's contemplation at Hira shows. Fatir links reverence to understanding creation, so Muslims should never shy away from science. He closes by urging full effort in the last ten nights.

outline.heading: A cluster on submission and obedience
outline.gist: Obedience is what Allah requires of us, but it is more profound than it seems, and each surah unpacks it from a different angle.

outline.heading: Al-Ahzab: obeying when it is hardest
outline.gist: Obeying Allah when there are many reasons not to is the way out of every difficulty and from darkness to light.

outline.heading: Saba: how a community obeys
outline.gist: Communal obedience looks different from individual obedience and has its own measures; few surahs address it.

outline.heading: Fatir: obedience through knowledge
outline.gist: Allah cannot be obeyed through ignorance; dignity comes from obeying Him the way He wants, not the way we want.

outline.heading: Ya-Sin: life is more than breathing
outline.gist: Real life is living with purpose and obeying Allah; an indifferent person who eats and drinks is spiritually dead, while the believing man of the town lives on.

outline.heading: Why Ya-Sin is read at death: the life of the spirit
outline.gist: The custom has no firm evidence, but he sees it as recognising that true life and death are of the spirit, which needs Allah as the body needs food.

outline.heading: No option once Allah and His Messenger decide
outline.gist: The central verse: a true believer does not see a ruling from Allah as one choice among several or as a matter for dispute.

outline.heading: The command is not hard; we are
outline.gist: The nafs resists what is selfless and beneficial and projects its difficulty onto commands; Allah has never commanded harm and wants ease for us.

outline.heading: Free to choose, yet obedience is not up for debate
outline.gist: Choice is a god-given right, but a believer does not treat disobedience as an option; some need reasons, while true believers obey and find the wisdom later.

outline.heading: Interlude
The trust the heavens, earth and mountains refused
outline.gist: The amanah is something held and returned unbroken: freedom of choice, which humanity took on and wronged itself with.

outline.heading: Only humans question their purpose
outline.gist: Tigers and salmon live their roles without doubt; only humans reflect on their motives, want more, and can say no to God.

outline.heading: Choices available, disobedience not among them
outline.gist: Other creatures choose within limits that exclude disobeying Allah, so they face no reward or punishment; we do.

outline.heading: Let children learn that choices matter
outline.gist: Shielding children too long and always bailing them out leaves them unable to value decisions; they must see consequences to carry the trust.

outline.heading: Communities obey through healthy dialogue
outline.gist: No society survives unless its groups learn to debate and disagree in a healthy way.

outline.heading: Either we or you are rightly guided
outline.gist: The Quran is not hesitating; entering a debate already closed to any argument is not dialogue and not Islamic.

outline.heading: A creed that follows the evidence
outline.gist: Muslims commit to follow the stronger proof, wherever it leads, even against inherited beliefs; only falsehood has reason to fear this.

outline.heading: Nothing in Islam is followed blindly
outline.gist: Those afraid of this lack trust in what they hold; every belief should rest on an intelligent argument.

outline.heading: Certainty, not probability, saves you
outline.gist: When life squeezes you, a faith that is only probably true will not hold; certainty built from clear argument will.

outline.heading: A book confident enough to say: let evidence decide
outline.gist: Only the owner of truth would invite this; the Prophet was always ready to debate, and Muslims struggle today because they lost that confidence.

outline.heading: Just one thing: rise for Allah in pairs or alone
outline.gist: Of all the advice, one request: dedicate yourself to discerning truth from falsehood, a kind of activism, together or individually.

outline.heading: Then reflect deeply
outline.gist: An hour of real contemplation outweighs a year of mindless worship because it shapes the values behind behaviour.

outline.heading: Fix the root cause, not the symptom
outline.gist: Lack of khushoo reflects something missing in belief or unresolved doubt; forced tears do not last, but rewiring conviction changes everything.

outline.heading: Your companion is not mad: where reflection leads
outline.gist: Honest contemplation concludes that the Prophet was truthful and a warner of what lies ahead.

outline.heading: Hira: the Prophet's prayer was contemplation
outline.gist: Before revelation he sat in a cave overlooking the Kaaba, plains and sky, asking why all this exists; without reflection something stays missing.

outline.heading: Diversity in fruits, mountains and peoples
outline.gist: Water brings forth varied fruits; rocks come in white, red and black; humans and animals in many colours and kinds.

outline.heading: Which scholars revere Allah?
outline.gist: Religious scholars explain the verse, but its context points to those who study creation; understanding what He made, down to a single cell, produces awe.

outline.heading: We have barely scratched the surface
outline.gist: Creation is not magic; the more one studies the body, immunology or ecosystems, the more one sees how little we know and how great the Maker is.

outline.heading: Never shy away from science because of religion
outline.gist: Belief comes through philosophy, reverence through knowing creation; learn your deen and every science.

outline.heading: Giving life to the last ten nights
outline.gist: The Prophet stayed up the whole night in the last ten and woke his family, which he did not do at other times.

outline.heading: Laylat al-Qadr is hidden
outline.gist: There is evidence for every one of the ten nights, because Allah hides it as He hides the day of death and which deeds He accepts.

outline.heading: Worship Him selfishly, through selflessness
outline.gist: No one asks you to worship selflessly; but the only way to secure your own acceptance is through service.

outline.heading: Mud on his forehead on the twenty-first night
outline.gist: It once fell on the twenty-first, which is tonight; treat the ten nights like an exam where one unknown question decides the result.

outline.heading: Outro

JT1wVa3qLO4.title: Building Taqwa and Closeness to Allah
JT1wVa3qLO4.one_line: Final Ramadan khutbah: keep striving to the last minute, seek Allah's pardon in the last nights, stay near Him after Ramadan, and give at Eid.
JT1wVa3qLO4.summary: With Eid a week away, he insists Ramadan is not over until Maghrib on its last day, and no Muslim may despair of Allah's mercy. The Prophet modelled this at Mina, staying through the last day of tashreeq after some two dozen tribes rejected him, and meeting six young men from Yathrib. In the last ten nights he exerted himself as at no other time and woke his family, and companions' dreams pointed to the last seven nights. Since the Generous has opened His doors, ask big: the Prophet taught Aisha to ask for pardon. Forgiven sins remain in your book and must be read out on Judgment Day, while pardoned sins are erased as though they never happened. Ramadan builds taqwa by keeping Allah in mind all day, and the verse that He is near is not seasonal: Allah never leaves after Ramadan, we are the ones who walk away. Even fatigue now earns reward. In the second khutbah he describes i'tikaf as a mindset of being devoted only to Allah for ten nights, even while working. He explains zakat al-fitr, which purifies the fast and feeds the poor, and urges giving well beyond it, because Muslims celebrate by giving and no one can out-give Allah.

outline.heading: Opening
It's not over until it's over
outline.gist: Some will hear a khutbah for the last time. Until Maghrib on the last day of Ramadan it is not over: whatever was wasted earlier, as long as one second remains you can still be accepted, and a Muslim may never despair of Allah's mercy.

outline.heading: Rejected by 26 tribes, he stayed to the end
outline.gist: In the tenth year of prophethood the Prophet was rejected by over 26 tribes during the days at Mina, yet stayed through the third and last day of tashreeq until almost no one was left.

outline.heading: Six young men waiting for a haircut
outline.gist: The last group to leave Mina were six young men from Yathrib, made to wait their turn for a haircut because no one gave the young priority; his conversation with them began the story of Madinah. Stand until the last second.

outline.heading: His effort in the last ten nights
outline.gist: With six or seven nights left: the Prophet exerted himself in the last ten nights as he did at no other time of the year, and we should do the same.

outline.heading: Waking his family
outline.gist: He kept every night alive but slept part of it; in the last ten he barely slept, woke his wife and went round waking Fatima, because loving someone means not letting them miss these nights, and he tightened his waist-wrap, a figure for full effort.

outline.heading: Seek it in the last seven nights
outline.gist: In Bukhari, companions saw in dreams that the Night of Decree was in the last seven nights; the Prophet said their dreams agreed, so whoever seeks it should seek it there.

outline.heading: When the Generous opens His doors, ask big
outline.gist: Asked what to say if she witnessed that night, he taught Aisha to ask for pardon: when the Generous opens His doors you do not dream small, you ask for the ultimate.

outline.heading: Forgiven sins stay in your book
outline.gist: On the Day of Judgment, as you hopefully take your book in your right hand, forgiven sins are still written there with the stamp of forgiveness on top.

outline.heading: Pardoned sins never happened
outline.gist: Read your book (17:14): forgiven sins must be read aloud and owned. A pardoned sin is gone from the book; the angels who recorded it and the people who witnessed it forget it, and only Allah knows it ever happened.

outline.heading: Sins you could not bear to read aloud
outline.gist: If there are sins you would be mortified to read in front of anyone, these are the nights, when Allah opens His doors as wide as they will ever be.

outline.heading: He loves to pardon
outline.gist: He loves to pardon; you need only be the right person at the right time. Push yourself for ten nights and show intention, commitment and desire for what Allah has hidden for you.

outline.heading: A month of living with Allah
outline.gist: Ramadan builds taqwa and closeness: for a month every movement connects you to Allah, so you taste the sweetness of it and want it to continue. That is why fasting was prescribed, that you may attain taqwa (2:183).

outline.heading: 'I am near' is not seasonal
outline.gist: When My servants ask about Me, I am near (2:186): He has always been near and listening, and the promise to answer dua does not end with Ramadan. He does not leave; we walk away.

outline.heading: Another chance every year
outline.gist: We are the ones who stop praying, coming to the masjid and reciting; Allah gives another Ramadan and another chance because He wants you near. Contemplate that in these nights.

outline.heading: Stay with Him to the last breath
outline.gist: Stay with Him as the Prophet did, until the last breath exhaled with the love of Allah, never closing the doors He opened. Renew your intentions today.

outline.heading: Even your fatigue earns reward
outline.gist: You are tired, hungry and sleep-deprived, but this is one of the few times in life that fatigue itself is rewarded, because it comes from worship for the sake of Allah.

outline.heading: Interlude
What i'tikaf means
outline.gist: I'tikaf means total focus: preoccupied with one thing and distracted by nothing else, as the Quran uses the word. You go to the masjid thinking of one thing only, as if stamped like an endowment for the sake of Allah.

outline.heading: I'tikaf even while working
outline.gist: Whether you sleep in the masjid or go to work to support your family, you can live the concept: for these ten nights everything else waits and all you say and do aims at closeness to Allah.

outline.heading: Stand in line until the doors close
outline.gist: When the Generous opens His doors, those truly in need stand in line until they close, and He never turns anyone away; not caring for what He offers would be almost disrespectful. The Prophet made zakat al-fitr obligatory on every Muslim, free or slave, male or female, young or old.

outline.heading: Zakat al-fitr: when and for whom
outline.gist: It is due before the Eid prayer, and most schools allow paying it from now. The head of the family pays for each member, counting a pregnancy, especially past four months.

outline.heading: Purifying the fast
outline.gist: About fifteen dollars a head, due from anyone with a day's food, unlike zakat with its year-long threshold. It purifies the fast from wrong words and deeds and makes up for its shortcomings.

outline.heading: Children without Eid
outline.gist: It also feeds the poor, because many Muslim children cannot enjoy Eid: no new clothes, no money for what their friends have, in an ummah of two billion.

outline.heading: We celebrate by giving
outline.gist: This ummah has never been wealthier, yet some children will wake on Eid heartbroken. Teach your children that Muslims celebrate by giving, not taking: zakat al-fitr before the prayer, sacrifice and feeding at the next Eid.

outline.heading: Zakat al-fitr is the least
outline.gist: Sixty or a hundred dollars for a family is the minimum; give as much as you can, locally and where war and disaster strike, so no one wakes on Eid feeling less than others.

outline.heading: You can't out-give Allah
outline.gist: Be generous in these days and Allah will be more generous: come a couple of metres closer and He comes kilometres, walk to Him and He comes running.

outline.heading: Outro

39:67.ar: وَمَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدۡرِهِۦ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ جَمِيعࣰ ا قَبۡضَتُهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ مَطۡوِيَّٰتُۢ بِيَمِينِهِۦۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
39:67.en: And they esteem not Allah as He hath the right to be esteemed, when the whole earth is His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens are rolled in His right hand. Glorified is He and High Exalted from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him)

40:39.en: O my people! Lo! this life of the world is but a passing comfort, and lo! the Hereafter, that is the enduring home

40:40.ar: مَنۡ عَمِلَ سَيِّئَةࣰ فَلَا يُجۡزَىٰٓ إِلَّا مِثۡلَهَاۖ وَمَنۡ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوۡ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنࣱ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يَدۡخُلُونَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ يُرۡزَقُونَ فِيهَا بِغَيۡرِ حِسَابࣲ‏
40:40.en: Whoso doeth an ill-deed, he will be repaid the like thereof, while whoso doeth right, whether male or female, and is a believer, (all) such will enter the Garden, where they will be nourished without stint

40:41.ar: ۞وَيَٰقَوۡمِ مَا لِيٓ أَدۡعُوكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلنَّجَوٰةِ وَتَدۡعُونَنِيٓ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِ
40:41.en: And, O my people! What aileth me that I call you unto deliverance when ye call me unto the Fire

40:42.ar: تَدۡعُونَنِي لِأَكۡفُرَ بِٱللَّهِ وَأُشۡرِكَ بِهِۦ مَا لَيۡسَ لِي بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣱ وَأَنَا۠ أَدۡعُوكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡغَفَّٰرِ
40:42.en: Ye call me to disbelieve in Allah and ascribe unto Him as partners that whereof I have no knowledge, while I call you unto the Mighty, the Forgiver

40:43.ar: لَا جَرَمَ أَنَّمَا تَدۡعُونَنِيٓ إِلَيۡهِ لَيۡسَ لَهُۥ دَعۡوَةࣱ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَلَا فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ وَأَنَّ مَرَدَّنَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأَنَّ ٱلۡمُسۡرِفِينَ هُمۡ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ
40:43.en: Assuredly that whereunto ye call me hath no claim in the world or in the Hereafter, and our return will be unto Allah, and the prodigals will be owners of the Fire

40:44.ar: فَسَتَذۡكُرُونَ مَآ أَقُولُ لَكُمۡۚ وَأُفَوِّضُ أَمۡرِيٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بَصِيرُۢ بِٱلۡعِبَادِ
40:44.en: And ye will remember what I say unto you. I confide my cause unto Allah. Lo! Allah is Seer of (His) slaves

40:45.ar: فَوَقَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِ مَا مَكَرُواْۖ وَحَاقَ بِـَٔالِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ سُوٓءُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ
40:45.en: So Allah warded off from him the evils which they plotted, while a dreadful doom encompassed Pharaoh's folk

40:60.ar: وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ٱدۡعُونِيٓ أَسۡتَجِبۡ لَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ عَنۡ عِبَادَتِي سَيَدۡخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دَاخِرِينَ
40:60.en: And your Lord hath said: Pray unto Me and I will hear your prayer. Lo! those who scorn My service, they will enter hell, disgraced

41:33.ar: وَمَنۡ أَحۡسَنُ قَوۡلࣰ ا مِّمَّن دَعَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا وَقَالَ إِنَّنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
41:33.en: And who is better in speech than him who prayeth unto his Lord and doeth right, and saith: Lo! I am of those who are muslims (surrender unto Him)

41:34.ar: وَلَا تَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡحَسَنَةُ وَلَا ٱلسَّيِّئَةُۚ ٱدۡفَعۡ بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِي بَيۡنَكَ وَبَيۡنَهُۥ عَدَٰوَةࣱ كَأَنَّهُۥ وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمࣱ‏
41:34.en: The good deed and the evil deed are not alike. Repel the evil deed with one which is better, then lo! he, between whom and thee there was enmity (will become) as though he was a bosom friend

41:35.ar: وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُواْ وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمࣲ‏
41:35.en: But none is granted it save those who are steadfast, and none is granted it save the owner of great happiness

28:20.ar: وَجَآءَ رَجُلࣱ مِّنۡ أَقۡصَا ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ يَسۡعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱلۡمَلَأَ يَأۡتَمِرُونَ بِكَ لِيَقۡتُلُوكَ فَٱخۡرُجۡ إِنِّي لَكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ
28:20.en: And a man came from the uttermost part of the city, running. He said: O Moses! Lo! the chiefs take counsel against thee to slay thee; therefor escape. Lo! I am of those who give thee good advice

25:77.ar: قُلۡ مَا يَعۡبَؤُاْ بِكُمۡ رَبِّي لَوۡلَا دُعَآؤُكُمۡۖ فَقَدۡ كَذَّبۡتُمۡ فَسَوۡفَ يَكُونُ لِزَامَۢا
25:77.en: Say (O Muhammad, unto the disbelievers): My Lord would not concern Himself with you but for your prayer. But now ye have denied (the Truth), therefor there will be judgment

aCV6ldObDg0.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 23: Quranic Reflections (Al-Zumar to Al-Shura)
aCV6ldObDg0.one_line: Opening the Ha-Mim cluster on dawah: Allah's majesty on the Last Day, the believer of Pharaoh's family, dua as worship, and dawah through character.
aCV6ldObDg0.summary: After al-Zumar's lesson that sincerity is the summit of obedience, he opens the Ha-Mim surahs, a cluster on dawah: stay connected to Allah, call through character, organize and work together, avoid materialism, delusion and arrogance, and accept that outcomes are Allah's. The verse of the earth in Allah's grip, which shook the Prophet on the minbar, shows that it was, is and will be only Allah; no one else is the hero of any story, and our helplessness on that Day is our reality now. The believer in Pharaoh's court called his people with simple truths about a fleeting world and a lasting Hereafter, knowing he might be killed, which shows dawah needs no great learning. Allah's promise to answer dua is joined to a warning for those too arrogant to worship, because dua is the essence of worship; he urges people to learn continuous dua in the remaining nights. Finally, 'who is better in speech' includes good deeds because actions speak louder: a famous Muslim athlete can do more against Islamophobia than years of lessons, so excel where Allah placed you. Repel evil with what is better, as the Prophet did with his persecutors, and make these verses a practice, not an anthem.

outline.heading: Opening
Al-Zumar: obedience through sincerity
outline.gist: After tawhid no practice matters more than sincerity, which is why intentions matter in everything we do.

outline.heading: The Ha-Mim cluster: carrying dawah to others
outline.gist: Unlike the earlier cluster on living the message, these surahs are about explaining Islam and bringing people closer to Allah.

outline.heading: Ghafir: stay connected while you call
outline.gist: You cannot take dawah to those who argue unless you are humble and practising yourself.

outline.heading: Fussilat: dawah through character
outline.gist: Years of talks do less than someone whose ethics and conduct speak for Islam; never underestimate your influence.

outline.heading: You need not memorize everything to call
outline.gist: Bringing Islam's values into your life is the best dawah, whatever you have memorized.

outline.heading: Al-Shura: unity and organization
outline.gist: Dawah needs togetherness, joint effort and consultation, which he compares loosely to democracy.

outline.heading: What hinders dawah: materialism, delusion, arrogance
outline.gist: Al-Zukhruf warns against materialism, al-Dukhan against misreading events, al-Jathiyah against arrogance even in the knowledgeable.

outline.heading: Al-Ahqaf: you cannot control the outcome
outline.gist: Do your part with connection, character and organization; who responds is in Allah's hands and will surprise you.

outline.heading: They did not esteem Allah as He deserves
outline.gist: The earth will be in His grip and the heavens folded in His right hand; the Prophet recited this from the minbar.

outline.heading: The horn, and the call: where are the kings?
outline.gist: Everything living dies, then Allah declares Himself the King and asks where the kings and tyrants of the earth are.

outline.heading: The minbar shook beneath him
outline.gist: As he described the Day when nothing remains but Allah, the minbar trembled as if it would fall.

outline.heading: It is only Allah, even now
outline.gist: It was always and will always be only Allah, and even with our existence it is only Him; we are a short ride on a small planet.

outline.heading: No one else is the hero of any story
outline.gist: Our helplessness on that Day is our reality today; we are just as in need of Him now and only live an illusion otherwise.

outline.heading: Where are the tyrants now?
outline.gist: The powerful never really had power; read these verses and those around them slowly.

outline.heading: The believer in Pharaoh's court
outline.gist: A believer among Pharaoh's inner circle of advisers speaks up in these verses.

outline.heading: The man who warned Musa to flee
outline.gist: He was the one who told Musa of the plot to kill him, sending him to Madyan, marriage and revelation; on Musa's return he still hid his faith.

outline.heading: This world is only brief enjoyment
outline.gist: Follow me and I will guide you: worldly pleasures are short-lived moments that fade and never fulfil.

outline.heading: Simple truths are enough for dawah
outline.gist: The Hereafter is the permanent home; the man had little knowledge or time with Musa, and the basic truths of existence were all he needed.

outline.heading: Interlude
Calling to salvation with what everyone knows
outline.gist: Righteous deeds by man or woman with faith lead to Paradise; why do you call me to the Fire?

outline.heading: I entrust my affair to Allah
outline.gist: He spoke knowing he would likely be killed, and Allah protected him.

outline.heading: Call upon Me and I will respond
outline.gist: A guaranteed promise that fits the last nights of Ramadan.

outline.heading: Why the promise ends with a warning
outline.gist: Those too arrogant to worship will enter Hell humbled; the two halves seem unrelated but are tightly connected.

outline.heading: Dua is the essence of worship
outline.gist: Every ritual exists so you can speak to Allah; prayer, recitation and remembrance are all forms of dua.

outline.heading: Not making dua is arrogance
outline.gist: Allah sets dua against arrogance in worship, and on reflection the comparison is exact.

outline.heading: Who else could answer you?
outline.gist: He invites you at any hour and guarantees a response; turning away when no one else can help makes no sense.

outline.heading: A command, a promise and a warning
outline.gist: Like the closing verse of al-Furqan, it shows that without a relationship with Allah even a good person is lost.

outline.heading: Learn dua as a lifelong conversation
outline.gist: Dua matters because it is continuous until you meet Allah; rituals without conversation are just going through the motions.

outline.heading: Dawah through behaviour is better
outline.gist: Clarity and articulation are needed, but the best dawah comes through practice.

outline.heading: Who is better in speech?
outline.gist: Allah says better spoken, then names calling to Him and doing good deeds, counting deeds as speech.

outline.heading: Actions speak louder than words
outline.gist: The volume of your actions is far higher than your words; a clip of his on this point circulated out of context.

outline.heading: One punch outweighed years of lessons
outline.gist: A famous Muslim fighter had more impact than hundreds of hours of teaching; be the best Muslim wherever Allah placed you.

outline.heading: Not everyone needs a microphone
outline.gist: One truly good Muslim who excels at his work under the banner of Islam has more impact.

outline.heading: A footballer and Islamophobia in the UK
outline.gist: A study credited a Muslim footballer who simply did his job well and was visibly Muslim with reducing Islamophobia.

outline.heading: Excel at whatever you do; the Prophet spoke little
outline.gist: Taxi driver or teacher, excel as a Muslim; the Prophet used few, carefully chosen words.

outline.heading: People followed how he lived
outline.gist: His generosity, humility and loyalty won people; perhaps that is why not one of his khutbahs survives in full.

outline.heading: Repel evil with what is better
outline.gist: Good and bad are never equal; answer what people throw at you with the best you have.

outline.heading: Try it on the person your nafs refuses
outline.gist: An enemy can become an intimate friend; start with the one person you would never do it for.

outline.heading: It almost never fails, and is almost never practised
outline.gist: We love reciting the verse but rarely live it because it is hard; look at the Prophet's life.

outline.heading: How the Prophet won over his persecutors
outline.gist: He met their cruelty with kindness until buried human decency surfaced and they believed.

outline.heading: He never gave up hope
outline.gist: He kept hoping for people who insulted and demeaned him, because good and evil are not equal.

outline.heading: Only the patient and the generously gifted
outline.gist: Only true perseverance and a great share of good character from Allah make this possible.

outline.heading: Isa: everyone gives what is inside him
outline.gist: Cursed in the street, Isa replied that each person produces what is in him, and he had only hope for people's guidance.

outline.heading: Verses are for practice, not anthems
outline.gist: We celebrate such verses to visitors but do not live them; if we are not practising them, that must become our priority.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.note: Sincerity is the most important practice after tawhid and the point of attending to intentions.

themes.label: Knowing Allah / relationship with Allah

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: This world is brief enjoyment and the Hereafter the permanent home, a truth simple enough for anyone to preach.

themes.label: Dua and invocation

41:37.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِ ٱلَّيۡلُ وَٱلنَّهَارُ وَٱلشَّمۡسُ وَٱلۡقَمَرُۚ لَا تَسۡجُدُواْ لِلشَّمۡسِ وَلَا لِلۡقَمَرِ وَٱسۡجُدُواْۤ لِلَّهِۤ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَهُنَّ إِن كُنتُمۡ إِيَّاهُ تَعۡبُدُونَ
41:37.en: And of His portents are the night and the day and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or the moon; but prostrate to Allah Who created them, if it is in truth Him Whom ye worship

41:38.ar: فَإِنِ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ فَٱلَّذِينَ عِندَ رَبِّكَ يُسَبِّحُونَ لَهُۥ بِٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ وَهُمۡ لَا يَسۡـَٔمُونَ۩
41:38.en: But if they are too proud - still those who are with thy Lord glorify Him night and day, and tire not

41:39.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَنَّكَ تَرَى ٱلۡأَرۡضَ خَٰشِعَةࣰ فَإِذَآ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهَا ٱلۡمَآءَ ٱهۡتَزَّتۡ وَرَبَتۡۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَحۡيَاهَا لَمُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
41:39.en: And of His portents (is this): that thou seest the earth lowly, but when We send down water thereon it thrilleth and groweth. Lo! He Who quickeneth it is verily the Quickener of the Dead. Lo! He is Able to do all things

41:40.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُلۡحِدُونَ فِيٓ ءَايَٰتِنَا لَا يَخۡفَوۡنَ عَلَيۡنَآۗ أَفَمَن يُلۡقَىٰ فِي ٱلنَّارِ خَيۡرٌ أَم مَّن يَأۡتِيٓ ءَامِنࣰ ا يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۚ ٱعۡمَلُواْ مَا شِئۡتُمۡ إِنَّهُۥ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
41:40.en: Lo! those who distort Our revelations are not hid from Us. Is he who is hurled into the Fire better, or he who cometh secure on the Day of Resurrection? Do what ye will. Lo! He is Seer of what ye do

41:41.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِٱلذِّكۡرِ لَمَّا جَآءَهُمۡۖ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَكِتَٰبٌ عَزِيزࣱ‏
41:41.en: Lo! those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it cometh unto them (are guilty), for lo! it is an unassailable Scripture

41:42.ar: لَّا يَأۡتِيهِ ٱلۡبَٰطِلُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ يَدَيۡهِ وَلَا مِنۡ خَلۡفِهِۦۖ تَنزِيلࣱ مِّنۡ حَكِيمٍ حَمِيدࣲ‏
41:42.en: Falsehood cannot come at it from before it or from behind it. (It is) a revelation from the Wise, the Owner of Praise

41:43.ar: مَّا يُقَالُ لَكَ إِلَّا مَا قَدۡ قِيلَ لِلرُّسُلِ مِن قَبۡلِكَۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغۡفِرَةࣲ وَذُو عِقَابٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
41:43.en: Naught is said unto thee (Muhammad) save what was said unto the messengers before thee. Lo! thy Lord is owner of forgiveness, and owner (also) of dire punishment

41:33.ar: وَمَنۡ أَحۡسَنُ قَوۡلࣰ ا مِّمَّن دَعَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا وَقَالَ إِنَّنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
41:33.en: And who is better in speech than him who prayeth unto his Lord and doeth right, and saith: Lo! I am of those who are muslims (surrender unto Him)

41:34.ar: وَلَا تَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡحَسَنَةُ وَلَا ٱلسَّيِّئَةُۚ ٱدۡفَعۡ بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِي بَيۡنَكَ وَبَيۡنَهُۥ عَدَٰوَةࣱ كَأَنَّهُۥ وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمࣱ‏
41:34.en: The good deed and the evil deed are not alike. Repel the evil deed with one which is better, then lo! he, between whom and thee there was enmity (will become) as though he was a bosom friend

41:35.ar: وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُواْ وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمࣲ‏
41:35.en: But none is granted it save those who are steadfast, and none is granted it save the owner of great happiness

41:36.ar: وَإِمَّا يَنزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ نَزۡغࣱ فَٱسۡتَعِذۡ بِٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
41:36.en: And if a whisper from the devil reach thee (O Muhammad) then seek refuge in Allah. Lo! He is the Hearer, the Knower

2:34.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأٓدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:34.en: And when We said unto the angels: Prostrate yourselves before Adam, they fell prostrate, all save Iblis. He demurred through pride, and so became a disbeliever

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

OnSiSxri-pg.title: Tafseer of Surat Fussilat, Part 6 (41:37-43)
OnSiSxri-pg.one_line: Signs in the universe and in the book: prostrate only to their Creator, see life from rain, and trust a Quran untouched by falsehood.
OnSiSxri-pg.summary: After recapping the surah's three points, he turns to two kinds of signs. Night and day, sun and moon are signs, not proofs: no equation equals God, but many signs pointing one way are as convincing as proof, like circumstantial evidence. Their precise tuning exists so that someone is here to reflect on them, and the simplest, most taken-for-granted things are where Allah is seen. Prostration symbolises admitting superiority, so do not prostrate to any sign, only to their Creator; the angels' prostration to Adam showed how Allah honoured humanity, against Iblis's argument from origin. Those in Allah's presence glorify Him tirelessly, so worship is for our own self-discovery and potential, not His need. The earth, humbled and lifeless, stirs and swells with rain and brings forth green, as time-lapses and deserts show, and the One who revives it revives the dead. Those who deviate regarding the signs are not hidden from Allah; 'do what you will' affirms free choice and different fates. You cannot control who listens, so hold yourself to the standard of verse 33, and those raised Muslim must contemplate harder. The Quran is unique and preserved, with no falsehood in it, and the objections raised against it are the same recycled arguments the earlier prophets heard.

outline.heading: A sign needs someone to reflect on it

outline.heading: Precisely tuned for us to exist
outline.gist: Had the earth rotated faster or slower, or the sun and moon been nearer or larger, no one would be here to reflect.

outline.heading: Do not prostrate to the signs

outline.gist: Iblis argued from origin since Adam had done nothing yet; the prostration shows Allah already ranked humans highly and placed great potential in them.

outline.heading: Submit only to Allah
outline.gist: Admit superiority only to the One who created all of these.

outline.heading: Arrogance, and those who never tire of glorifying
outline.gist: Arrogance runs through all seven surahs of this cluster; those near Allah glorify Him night and day without boredom.

outline.heading: Worship is for you, not for Him
outline.gist: Allah does not need our worship; it is for us to understand who we are and why we are here.

outline.heading: Self-discovery and limitless potential
outline.gist: Small and fragile in a corner of the universe, a person who discovers their purpose can encompass far more than their size.

outline.heading: Not His loss but ours
outline.gist: If someone is too arrogant to prostrate, Allah loses nothing; others exalt Him constantly.

outline.heading: The humbled earth stirs and swells
outline.gist: Lifeless land looks beaten and humble; time-lapses show it shaking and swelling when rain falls, then turning green.

outline.heading: Life in the desert, and the blessing of being alive
outline.gist: In the desert green appears before your eyes after rain; nothing is a bigger blessing than life, to which we contribute almost nothing.

outline.heading: If seeds stopped accepting water
outline.gist: We understand how seeds grow but not why; if they stopped, no biologist could do anything.

outline.heading: He who revives the earth revives the dead
outline.gist: The signs are of two kinds: those on the page of creation and those in the book He sent.

outline.heading: Muslims must also contemplate both kinds of signs
outline.gist: Faith received as a child must be built up with reflection later in life if it is to stay.

outline.heading: Those who deviate regarding Our signs
outline.gist: Ilhad is refusing to see the signs as having an origin or reading them from a different angle; they are not hidden from Allah.

outline.heading: Thrown in the Fire or secure on the Day?
outline.gist: Allah will not combine two fears or two securities for His servant: fear Him here and be safe there.

outline.heading: Do what you will; He sees what you do
outline.gist: Not permission for sin but a statement of free choice, with the reminder that the two groups will not be equal.

outline.heading: Those who reject the reminder: a sentence left open
outline.gist: The verse omits its predicate, leaving the listener to fill in the consequence, as in the previous verse.

outline.heading: You cannot control who listens
outline.gist: Some will not believe whatever signs they see; do not exhaust yourself, return to the central verse and hold yourself to it.

outline.heading: Gratitude for being guided
outline.gist: If Allah granted you understanding and commitment, praise Him constantly, since others cannot find the way.

outline.heading: Born Muslim? Contemplate harder
outline.gist: Having skipped the initial search, one should reflect more deeply to make up for it.

outline.heading: All Islamic scholarship serves understanding His words
outline.gist: Every book, lesson and grammar class is a modest effort to understand what Allah said so it can be practised.

outline.heading: A mighty, unique book
outline.gist: 'Aziz means there is nothing like it and nothing can reach it; no scripture has been studied in such detail.

outline.heading: Care down to the sound of each letter
outline.gist: Recitation is preserved to the finest detail of articulation, corrected at the slightest deviation.

outline.heading: Falsehood cannot approach it from before or behind
outline.gist: There is no error or flaw by which falsehood could enter it.

outline.heading: The only pure truth
outline.gist: Every other book, even of hadith, contains some error; the Quran alone is pure truth in past, present and future.

outline.heading: Sent down from the Wise, the Praiseworthy
outline.gist: Being able to hold and believe in it is itself a reason to praise Him.

outline.heading: Nothing is said to you but what was said before
outline.gist: Scholars split on whether it means Allah's message or the disbelievers' objections; he favours the latter.

outline.heading: The same recycled arguments
outline.gist: Every argument against God can be traced back thousands of years; it is philosophy, not science, and nothing new.

outline.heading: Keep articulating and do not be upset
outline.gist: Continue explaining; your Lord is the Owner of forgiveness and of painful punishment.

outline.heading: Outro

E_Njg5NTLIM.title: Facing Disbelief 1: Reasons for Disbelief, Common Fallacies and the Sources of Eman
E_Njg5NTLIM.one_line: Six reasons people lose faith, eight logical fallacies used on both sides, and the four sources of evidence on which eman rests.
E_Njg5NTLIM.summary: Opening a series on facing disbelief in the modern context, he argues that classical works answered their own era well but Muslims now need tools suited to a scientific age. He sets out six reasons people leave faith, drawn from surveys: bad behaviour by religious people, cognitive dissonance when inherited beliefs meet undeniable facts, politicising sacred texts, witnessing oppression, groups like ISIS, and four mentalities: mechanistic thinking that denies intuition, metaphor blindness, intolerance of uncertainty, and the Nirvana fallacy of setting the standard God must meet. He then teaches eight fallacies, stressing that believers use them as much as disbelievers: ad hominem, straw man, red herring, appeal to numbers and its snob reverse, appeal to emotion, the historian's fallacy, and the complex question. Looking for God in science is like fishing in a swimming pool: anything science could prove would be inside space-time and so not God. Science instead offers signs, which is why the Quran speaks of ayat. Eman is belief based on overwhelming converging evidence from four sources: the universe, life, history and personal experience, as a court convicts on converging evidence without footage. In questions he addresses free will, scientism and why evidence, not physical proof, is how science itself works.

outline.heading: Opening
Why classical answers need updating
outline.gist: Classical scholars addressed disbelief well for their times, but a century of scientific change and confusion between disciplines requires new tools.

outline.heading: Aim of the series and its sources
outline.gist: This first session's fallacies are the vocabulary for the rest; he draws on Hamza Tzortzis, Martin Rees's Just Six Numbers, an Arabic work and his own material.

outline.heading: Reason one: bad behaviour of the religious
outline.gist: The leading reason people leave faith, per surveys, is seeing dishonesty or lack of commitment in those who preach it.

outline.heading: Who the series is for
outline.gist: Not for those whose minds are made up, but for believers who struggle and those in the grey zone seeking a sound rationale.

outline.heading: Bad behaviour at home and in the masjid
outline.gist: Parents who do the opposite of what they command, imams who preach one thing and practise another; we can complain or acknowledge and address it.

outline.heading: Reason two: cognitive dissonance
outline.gist: When an undeniable fact clashes with an inherited belief, one can follow the truth, reconcile the two, or wall off the truth, which is the Quranic picture of kufr.

outline.heading: Reason three: politicising sacred texts
outline.gist: Using revelation for personal gain, loyalty or control is corruption, and people who see the hypocrisy step away from faith.

outline.heading: Reason four: oppression and brutality
outline.gist: Without psychological and theological preparation, witnessing torture and killing, as after the Arab Spring, drives people from belief.

outline.heading: Reason five: ISIS and its kin
outline.gist: Groups that hijack texts to kill on a mass scale, an old phenomenon going back to the Khawarij, are a leading cause of lost faith he witnessed himself.

outline.heading: Reason six: mentalities that lead to disbelief
outline.gist: A recap of the first five reasons and an introduction to four ways of thinking he worries about in the Muslim community.

outline.heading: Mentality one: mechanistic thinking
outline.gist: Accepting only what formulas and numbers show denies intuition and damages relationships as well as faith.

outline.heading: Science itself rests on intuition
outline.gist: Every hypothesis and major discovery begins as a hunch; the scientific method tests ideas but cannot generate them.

outline.heading: Mentality two: metaphor blindness
outline.gist: Reading everything literally, as in a literalist reading of the hadith that a virgin's consent is her silence, makes texts absurd and pushes people away.

outline.heading: Mentality three: uncertainty avoidance
outline.gist: All-or-nothing thinking; patients who cannot accept probabilities, and converts he watched radicalise and then leave Islam.

outline.heading: The deen holds designed uncertainty
outline.gist: Allah left some matters probabilistic, and most evidence outside the Quran sits between certain and rejected; faith needs a mind that sees grey.

outline.heading: Mentality four: the Nirvana fallacy
outline.gist: Setting one's own standard of mercy and rejecting God for not meeting it; the problem lies in the expectation, not in Allah.

outline.heading: What a fallacy is
outline.gist: A logical trick that makes something false look correct; he takes eight from modern philosophy.

outline.heading: Fallacy one: ad hominem
outline.gist: Attacking the person instead of the argument, as when a scholar's sound point is dismissed because of his past.

outline.heading: Fallacy two: straw man
outline.gist: Painting a flawed version of the other view and refuting that; among the most common fallacies used against Islam and by Muslims.

outline.heading: Fallacy three: red herring
outline.gist: Distracting from the point, such as jumping from God's existence to the Prophet's marriages; why a talk with a doubting teen takes hours, not minutes.

outline.heading: Fallacy four: appeal to numbers
outline.gist: Claiming truth because many believe it; Islam never measured truth by numbers, and the Prophet had few followers for thirteen years.

outline.heading: Fallacy five: the snob approach
outline.gist: Claiming truth because only a small elite holds it, as groups misuse the hadith of a small victorious group; both sides argue numbers, not evidence.

outline.heading: Fallacy six: appeal to emotion
outline.gist: Believers' most common fallacy; emotional preaching wins popularity but builds no foundation, while a sound argument later produces real emotion.

outline.heading: Fallacy seven: the historian's fallacy
outline.gist: Judging past people by present standards, illustrated with slavery in Arabia and with how future generations may judge our burning of fuel.

outline.heading: Fallacy eight: the complex question
outline.gist: Loaded questions with forced answers, like asking whether God can create a rock He cannot move, which misunderstands what creating means.

outline.heading: Fallacies in everyday life
outline.gist: Logic is rarely taught; divorced parents straw-man each other to children and spouses deploy red herrings when cornered.

outline.heading: Fishing for God in a swimming pool
outline.gist: Science studies only the observable universe within space-time, so anything it could prove would by definition not be God; philosophy reaches beyond.

outline.heading: Science gives signs, not proof
outline.gist: Science supplies arrows all pointing in one direction, which is why the Quran speaks of ayat, signs, rather than proofs.

outline.heading: The four sources of eman
outline.gist: The universe, life, history, and intuition or personal experience, the outline of the coming sessions.

outline.heading: Eman as belief on converging evidence
outline.gist: Like a court convicting on motive and testimony without footage, eman believes what overwhelming evidence points to without direct proof.

outline.heading: Why Allah does not simply appear
outline.gist: If Allah presented Himself there would be no test; angels who see the unseen are rarely described with eman.

outline.heading: Interlude
Ascending beyond evidence; is love real?
outline.gist: One starts with the evidence but grows into a personal relationship with Allah; the mechanistic mindset also leads to the growing claim that love is not real.

outline.heading: Free will and the neuroscientist
outline.gist: Denying choice makes debate pointless; collective behaviour is predictable, which is why laws exist, but individuals still choose.

outline.heading: Evidence, not proof, is how science works
outline.gist: Drugs are approved on repeated patterns of evidence without full understanding of mechanism.

outline.heading: Both camps of the numbers fallacy
outline.gist: Majority and elite groups argue their fallacy rather than the evidence, a pattern he has seen among Muslims.

outline.heading: The complex-terms fallacy
outline.gist: Burying a simple matter in jargon so the listener feels foolish, as rushed doctors sometimes do.

outline.heading: Slavery and judging by context
outline.gist: Slavery is wrong, but judging entire past populations without understanding their context is not sound; a later session will address it.

outline.heading: Start with the basics, in sequence
outline.gist: Never begin from emotion or personal experience; start with the universe, then life, history and finally personal experience.

outline.heading: Media portrayals of Islam as a straw man
outline.gist: A hard personal life does not disprove God. Western narratives choose pieces out of context to build a weak version of Islam they can knock down.

outline.heading: Scientism and the bullying of philosophy
outline.gist: Rejecting anything without physical proof is itself a fallacy; scientism denies philosophy, which built civilisations.

outline.heading: Even research rests on probabilities
outline.gist: P-values mean some findings are false positives; converging signs from every source, none contradicting, are more meaningful than one study.

38:23.ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَآ أَخِي لَهُۥ تِسۡعࣱ وَتِسۡعُونَ نَعۡجَةࣰ وَلِيَ نَعۡجَةࣱ وَٰحِدَةࣱ فَقَالَ أَكۡفِلۡنِيهَا وَعَزَّنِي فِي ٱلۡخِطَابِ
38:23.en: Lo! this my brother hath ninety and nine ewes while I had one ewe; and he said: Entrust it to me, and he conquered me in speech

38:24.ar: قَالَ لَقَدۡ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعۡجَتِكَ إِلَىٰ نِعَاجِهِۦۖ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡخُلَطَآءِ لَيَبۡغِي بَعۡضُهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَقَلِيلࣱ مَّا هُمۡۗ وَظَنَّ دَاوُۥدُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّٰهُ فَٱسۡتَغۡفَرَ رَبَّهُۥ وَخَرَّۤ رَاكِعࣰ اۤ وَأَنَابَ۩
38:24.en: (David) said: He hath wronged thee in demanding thine ewe in addition to his ewes, and lo! many partners oppress one another, save such as believe and do good works, and they are few. And David guessed that We had tried him, and he sought forgiveness of his Lord, and he bowed himself and fell down prostrate and repented

38:25.ar: فَغَفَرۡنَا لَهُۥ ذَٰلِكَۖ وَإِنَّ لَهُۥ عِندَنَا لَزُلۡفَىٰ وَحُسۡنَ مَـَٔابࣲ‏
38:25.en: So We forgave him that; and lo! he had access to Our presence and a happy journey's end

38:26.ar: يَٰدَاوُۥدُ إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَٰكَ خَلِيفَةࣰ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱحۡكُم بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ ٱلۡهَوَىٰ فَيُضِلَّكَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ شَدِيدُۢ بِمَا نَسُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
38:26.en: (And it was said unto him): O David! Lo! We have set thee as a viceroy in the earth; therefor judge aright between mankind, and follow not desire that it beguile thee from the way of Allah. Lo! those who wander from the way of Allah have an awful doom, forasmuch as they forgot the Day of Reckoning

39:17.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱجۡتَنَبُواْ ٱلطَّٰغُوتَ أَن يَعۡبُدُوهَا وَأَنَابُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ لَهُمُ ٱلۡبُشۡرَىٰۚ فَبَشِّرۡ عِبَادِ
39:17.en: And those who put away false gods lest they should worship them and turn to Allah in repentance, for them there are glad tidings. Therefor give good tidings (O Muhammad) to My bondmen

39:18.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَسۡتَمِعُونَ ٱلۡقَوۡلَ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ أَحۡسَنَهُۥٓۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمۡ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
39:18.en: Who hear advice and follow the best thereof. Such are those whom Allah guideth, and such are men of understanding

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

38:44.ar: وَخُذۡ بِيَدِكَ ضِغۡثࣰ ا فَٱضۡرِب بِّهِۦ وَلَا تَحۡنَثۡۗ إِنَّا وَجَدۡنَٰهُ صَابِرࣰ اۚ نِّعۡمَ ٱلۡعَبۡدُ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابࣱ‏
38:44.en: And (it was said unto him): Take in thine hand a branch and smite therewith, and break not thine oath. Lo! We found him steadfast, how excellent a slave! Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (to his Lord)

38:71.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي خَٰلِقُۢ بَشَرࣰ ا مِّن طِينࣲ‏
38:71.en: When thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to create a mortal out of mire

38:72.ar: فَإِذَا سَوَّيۡتُهُۥ وَنَفَخۡتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِي فَقَعُواْ لَهُۥ سَٰجِدِينَ
38:72.en: And when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My Spirit, then fall down before him prostrate

38:73.en: The angels fell down prostrate, every one

38:74.ar: إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
38:74.en: Saving Iblis; he was scornful and became one of the disbelievers

38:75.ar: قَالَ يَٰٓإِبۡلِيسُ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَن تَسۡجُدَ لِمَا خَلَقۡتُ بِيَدَيَّۖ أَسۡتَكۡبَرۡتَ أَمۡ كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلۡعَالِينَ
38:75.en: He said: O Iblis! What hindereth thee from falling prostrate before that which I have created with both My hands? Art thou too proud or art thou of the high exalted

38:76.ar: قَالَ أَنَا۠ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنۡهُ خَلَقۡتَنِي مِن نَّارࣲ وَخَلَقۡتَهُۥ مِن طِينࣲ‏
38:76.en: He said: I am better than him. Thou createdst me of fire, whilst him Thou didst create of clay

38:77.en: He said: Go forth from hence, for lo! thou art outcast

38:78.ar: وَإِنَّ عَلَيۡكَ لَعۡنَتِيٓ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلدِّينِ
38:78.en: And lo! My curse is on thee till the Day of Judgment

38:79.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ فَأَنظِرۡنِيٓ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ يُبۡعَثُونَ
38:79.en: He said: My Lord! Reprieve me till the day when they are raised

38:80.en: He said: Lo! thou art of those reprieved

112:1.en: Say: He is Allah, the One

112:2.en: Allah, the eternally Besought of all

112:3.en: He begetteth not nor was begotten

112:4.en: And there is none comparable unto Him

39:55.ar: وَٱتَّبِعُوٓاْ أَحۡسَنَ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكُم مِّن رَّبِّكُم مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَكُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ بَغۡتَةࣰ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تَشۡعُرُونَ
39:55.en: And follow the better (guidance) of that which is revealed unto you from your Lord, before the doom cometh on you suddenly when ye know not

oJ3vWtzqB0g.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 22: Quranic Reflections
oJ3vWtzqB0g.one_line: Reflections on Yasin, As-Saffat, Sad and Az-Zumar as a cluster on obeying Allah: spiritual life, companions, Ibrahim's submission, Dawud's repentance and sincerity.
oJ3vWtzqB0g.summary: He frames the surahs from al-Ahzab to az-Zumar as one cluster that looks at obedience to Allah from several angles: obeying when it is hard, obeying as a community, obeying through knowledge, obedience as the source of real life, obeying when the wisdom is unclear, returning after mistakes, and sincerity. From Yasin he argues that the Quran warns those who are truly alive, since a heart starved of its Lord dies and, like a starved body, needs time to revive. From As-Saffat he uses the believer in Paradise who tells his old friend he nearly ruined him, to urge people to audit their circle and guard time as their only capital. Ibrahim's dream of sacrificing his son shows full submission to a clear command with no visible wisdom; since Allah only ever commands what benefits us, complaining about fasting, hijab or salah makes little sense. Dawud's quick repentance after judging without hearing both sides defines the khalifah as someone who stands by truth and admits error without excuses. From Az-Zumar he teaches that sincerity decides how you do the right thing, such as giving advice in a way that draws people to Allah rather than scoring an 'I told you so'.

outline.heading: Opening
Al-Ahzab, Saba and Fatir: obeying in hardship, as a society, through knowledge
outline.gist: The cluster studies obedience from several angles: you show your true colours when obeying is hard, a community needs its own measures of obedience, and Allah is obeyed on His terms through proper learning.

outline.heading: Yasin: obedience as the source of real life
outline.gist: You can breathe and still not be alive; full life is the life of the spirit, knowing what you are here for and obeying Allah.

outline.heading: As-Saffat: obeying when the wisdom is unclear
outline.gist: A clear command is obeyed even when its reasoning is hidden, as with events that are hard to make sense of; the wisdom may become clear later.

outline.heading: Sad: returning after mistakes
outline.gist: Part of obedience is not being too proud to say you were wrong, going back, and making it public if needed.

outline.heading: Az-Zumar and sincerity: long, middle and short versions
outline.gist: Sincerity, the final key of obedience, is taught at length in one surah, more briefly in Az-Zumar and in a few words in Al-Ikhlas; the Quran teaches many concepts at these three depths.

outline.heading: Warning those who are truly alive
outline.gist: The Quran is not poetry; it warns the living, which cannot mean the biologically alive, since some of the dead are more alive among us than the living. A dead spirit hears nothing.

outline.heading: Alive set against the disbelievers: disbelief starves the spirit
outline.gist: The verse contrasts the living with the disbelievers rather than the dead, because rejecting Allah kills something inside; as fasting shows the body's hunger, the spirit craves its Lord and dies without Him.

outline.heading: Why we feel nothing in salah: reviving a starved spirit
outline.gist: A spirit deprived for years cannot respond at once; like refeeding a starved body it takes time, so be grateful to be somewhere it can be nourished.

outline.heading: The believer who was nearly ruined by his friend
outline.gist: A believer in Paradise recalls the companion who mocked belief in resurrection and tells him he almost brought him down, if not for his Lord's favour.

outline.heading: Audit your circle: even the saved came close to failing
outline.gist: Everyone is open to peer pressure at any age; use Ramadan to identify who draws you to Allah, slowly step back from those who don't, and be picky to the point of seeming arrogant.

outline.heading: Time is your only capital
outline.gist: Wealth comes and goes, but time spent never returns and cannot be bought or extended, so be careful what you spend it on and with whom.

outline.heading: Obey clear commands even when the reason is hidden
outline.gist: This applies to clear, authentic commands, not ambiguous ones: he need not know why pork is forbidden, and Ibrahim is the prime example.

outline.heading: A command no one could rationalise
outline.gist: Ibrahim is told to slaughter his son just as the boy reaches the age a father enjoys most; whether Ismail or Ishaq is a scholarly difference not worth fixating on, and a dream seen repeatedly by a prophet is revelation.

outline.heading: No conceivable wisdom, which is the point
outline.gist: There was no benefit in killing his son, which is why it never happened; it shows that Allah could command something without benefit but never has, and the son answers that his father should do as he is commanded.

outline.heading: 'Aslama': full submission
outline.gist: They were already Muslim; the word means they gave up every illusion of control and submitted completely, which pilgrims recall by slaughtering a ram.

outline.heading: The knife that would not cut, and the ransom
outline.gist: He narrates step by step as nothing stops it, until the stroke falls and the blade does not cut because Allah told it not to; a ram is given as ransom for the clear trial.

outline.heading: Shaytan's three temptations and the stoning at Hajj
outline.gist: Shaytan came to Ibrahim, to Ismail and to his mother, and each refused because the command was clear; pilgrims walk in their footsteps when they throw the pebbles.

outline.heading: He never commanded harm, so why complain
outline.gist: Allah only ever commands what benefits us in both lives; if we cannot stomach fasting, hijab and salah, we would never have done what Ibrahim did.

outline.heading: Khalifah, first heard: stand by truth at all costs
outline.gist: In order of revelation this is the first time the companions heard the word; its first pillar is to judge, speak and live by what is right whatever is on the other side of the scale.

outline.heading: Do not follow whims: without truth the deen is empty
outline.gist: The second pillar is refusing to follow the desires of the self; remove adherence to what is right and nothing of Islam is left.

outline.heading: Dawud and the two litigants: judging without hearing both sides
outline.gist: On his day set aside for worship two men climb into his private quarters; he rules for the man with one ewe against the brother with ninety-nine without hearing the other side.

outline.heading: Repenting without excuses, even in public
outline.gist: He was king, it was his day of worship and they trespassed, yet he gave himself no excuse and fell in repentance; Ayyub's oath and Iblis's refusal in the same surah show returning and refusing to return, and a true khalifah admits error even from the minbar.

outline.heading: Following the best of what is said: the right thing done the right way
outline.gist: Not that some of the Quran is better than the rest, but that every right action can be done in a way that serves its purpose or in a way that defeats it.

outline.heading: Sincerity decides how you give advice
outline.gist: Correcting someone publicly or condescendingly gives you the pleasure of 'I told you so' but pushes them away; sincerity makes you choose the way that brings them closer to Allah.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger
themes.note: Lays out the cluster as a study of obedience from difficulty, community, knowledge, life, unclear wisdom, returning and sincerity.

themes.label: Spirituality, khushoo and the inner life
themes.note: True life is the life of the spirit; a heart deprived of Allah stops hearing and needs patient revival, which is why many feel nothing in salah.

themes.label: Brotherhood, companionship and friendship
themes.note: Peer influence can nearly cost someone Paradise, so be picky about friends and slowly distance yourself from those who pull you away from Allah.

themes.label: Time, opportunity and seizing the moment
themes.note: Time is the only capital that cannot be regained or extended; spend it carefully and with the right people.

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger
themes.note: Ibrahim's sacrifice as the model of obeying a clear command without seeing its wisdom.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Ibrahim and Ismail's submission, and Dawud's judgment and repentance, read as lessons in obedience and returning.

themes.label: The purposes behind Allah's commands (maqasid)
themes.note: Allah could have commanded something with no benefit but never did; every command serves us in this life and the next.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: The khalifah judges and lives by truth at all costs and refuses to follow his whims.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Dawud admits error at once without excuses; a true khalifah takes mistakes back, even publicly, unlike Iblis.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: Sincerity is the final key of obedience and dictates the manner in which you do good.

themes.label: Commanding good and forbidding wrong (amr bil-ma'ruf)
themes.note: Correcting someone publicly or condescendingly feeds the ego; sincere advice is given in the way most likely to be accepted.

quran.point: Khalifah appears there first in mushaf order, though Sad 38:26 is where the companions first heard it in revelation order
Ayyub's oath about his wife as another prophet who erred and made it right
Iblis at the end of the surah as the one who erred and never took it back
The shortest version of the teaching on sincerity, beside Az-Zumar's fuller treatment
The idea of following the best of what is revealed appears twice in Az-Zumar

maxims: Real life is the life of the spirit
Your capital is your time
Be picky, borderline arrogant, about who you spend time with
He never told you to do anything harmful
The right thing, done the right way
We are only valuable by our adherence to what is right

stories.who: Believer in Paradise and his former companion (As-Saffat)
stories.point: Even the saved came close to being led astray by a friend; guard your circle.

stories.who: Ibrahim and Ismail: the dream of sacrifice
stories.point: Full submission to a clear command whose wisdom cannot be seen; Allah never actually commands harm.

stories.who: Shaytan tempting Ibrahim, Ismail and Hajar on the way
stories.point: Each refused because the command was clear; the stoning at Hajj walks in their footsteps.

stories.who: Dawud and the two litigants over the ewes
stories.point: He judged without hearing both sides, then repented immediately without leaning on his excuses.
One erred and returned; the other erred and never took it back.

takeaways: Use Ramadan to identify who in your close circle draws you to Allah and who doesn't, and slowly step back from the latter.
Treat your time as finite capital and be deliberate about how and with whom you spend it.
Obey clear commands even when you can't see the wisdom, and stop complaining about fasting, hijab and salah.
When you are wrong, admit it quickly, publicly if needed, without excuses.
Give advice privately and gently, in the way that brings the person closer to Allah, not to win the argument.
